title: Complete connector search coverage
prompt:
Work through the identified free-knowledge connectors in ddk220-light/MyBookshelf-web and get their searches working. Actively do the work each run and resume saved progress. Prioritize unchecked connectors and groups with the fewest working connectors.

Use three statuses: Working (real supported queries return relevant items, with saved examples and search scope), Blocked/failed (a specific reason prevents working queries), and Still checking. Queryability is the coverage goal; extra dossier, topic and country checklists must not hold up this count.

Investigate blockers. Fix connector mistakes, retry temporary failures with sensible backoff, or try a documented permitted API/export/search alternative when there is a good reason. Save the cause, attempt, result and next action. Do not blindly repeat failures or bypass access controls. Resume interrupted work only after confirming no other worker is active.

Every run, report here—even if nothing changed:
- A table for the six groups plus totals: Working | Blocked/failed | Still checking | Total.
- Changes since the previous report and how many remain to check.
- Blocked connector names, plain reasons, what was tried, and whether to retry, use another method, wait or ask me for help.
- What you are doing next, and a link to the per-connector status list.

Use the isolated research/free-content-discovery-expansion worktree. Fetch first; read AGENTS.md, docs/STATUS.md and the registry goal/status files. Follow the repository’s research validation workflow, preserve evidence and unrelated changes, and commit/push checkpoints. Keep connector-status.json/CSV and the goal current. Never duplicate an active writer or force push.

Research only: no production activation/deployment, paid services/accounts, bulk books/audio or personal-owner data. Respect provider policies and pacing. Keep this task enabled and continue across runs; a blocked provider is not a reason to stop.
